paper_metadata.title: Solving the Product Breakdown Structure Problem with constrained QAOA

experiments.description: Constrained QAOA for the PBS problem on randomly generated tree instances, benchmarked in simulation with 3 QAOA layers and varying problem sizes / tree structures.

algorithm.variant: Constrained QAOA with problem-specific state preparation and constrained mixer
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Trotterized Quantum Annealing (TQA) parameter initialization protocol

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Each of M parts is encoded as a QuantumVariable of N qubits in one-hot form (OHQInt(N)); total encoding uses M QuantumVariables and M·N qubits.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize C = sum_{(r,s) in phi} c^r_{f(r),f(s)} with f:[M]->[N] and c^r_{i,j} > 0, symmetric in i,j.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Constrained QAOA with feasible-subspace state preparation and a mixer that preserves feasibility; no penalty terms used in the implemented quantum approach.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Phase-separating operator generated from a SymPy polynomial for the classical cost function; no explicit Hamiltonian matrix form given.

problem_instance.description: Product Breakdown Structure (PBS) instances defined by rooted directed trees; benchmark instances include randomly generated tree graphs with maximum degree N = floor(M/2) for the scaling figure, and specific small trees in Figures 2 and 3.

dataset_specification.description: Randomly generated tree graphs for scaling study; 30 graphs per M. Benchmark instances shown include phi = {(1,0),(2,0),(3,0)} with N=4,5,6; phi = {(1,0),(2,0),(3,1)} with N=4; phi = {(1,0),(2,0),(3,0),(4,1)} with N=5; phi = {(1,0),(2,0),(3,0),(4,1),(5,1),(6,1)} with N=4.

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Simulator-based benchmarking on Qrisp; results reported as aggregated probabilities of measuring feasible solutions and success probability P0.1 for near-optimal solutions; varying number of QAOA layers from 0 to 4; 0 layers corresponds to uniform superposition of feasible solutions.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Cost function compiled from SymPy polynomial; PBS state preparation via recursive algorithm using partial W-states and controlled swaps; QAOA initialized with TQA.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Success probabilities and aggregated cost distributions computed from measurement outcomes; near-optimality assessed via C(f) < (1 + alpha) * Cmin.

results.unit: parts / tree nodes (scaling study maximum shown in figure)
orders of magnitude difference at M=20
N qubits per part in one-hot encoding

speedup_claims.factor: 46 orders of magnitude smaller search space at M=20
speedup_claims.baseline_method: quasi-constrained QUBO / full unconstrained search space
speedup_claims.conditions: for randomly generated tree instances with maximum degree N = floor(M/2) in the scaling figure
speedup_claims.caveats: This refers to state-space size reduction, not measured runtime or end-to-end solution quality.

speedup_claims.conditions: due to constrained subspace search and feasible-state preparation
speedup_claims.caveats: Claimed qualitatively; no direct runtime speedup benchmark against a classical solver is reported.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(p·M^2·N) gates and O(p·M·N) depth; state preparation O(M^2·N) gates and O(M·N) depth; constrained mixer depth reduced to O(log N) for the MCP component after exploiting structure.
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(M·N^(m+1)) for the dynamic programming baseline; for special cases: star tree O(N^M), chain O(M·N^2), binary tree O(M·N^3).

experiments.description: Barren plateau susceptibility study for the proposed constrained QAOA ansatz, using increasing PBS problem sizes and finite-difference gradient variance estimation.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Same one-hot QuantumArray encoding as the main PBS experiment; total qubits reported explicitly in Table 1 as Nq.
problem_formulation.objective_function: PBS cost function as defined in the paper; gradient variance is computed for the cost function of the proposed Ansatz.

problem_instance.description: PBS instances used only for gradient-variance scaling analysis.

dataset_specification.description: Table 1 instances with varying tree structures and qubit counts: 12, 16, 20, 24 qubits.

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Variance of the cost-function gradient computed with 100 samples; logarithmic plot shown in Figure 4.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Finite-difference gradient estimation with respect to the last variational parameter.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Variance computed from 100 gradient samples and plotted on a logarithmic scale.

convergence_data.variance_across_runs: Reported as decreasing variance with increasing problem size; exact values not tabulated in text.

classical_baselines.method_name: other variational algorithms affected by barren plateaus

speedup_claims.factor: suppressed barren plateau effect / less impactful variance decay
speedup_claims.baseline_method: generic variational algorithms with barren plateaus
speedup_claims.conditions: for increasing PBS problem sizes in the finite-difference gradient study
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports a qualitative/log-scale comparison; exact variance values are not tabulated in the text.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Not separately quantified for this gradient study beyond the main constrained-QAOA scaling.
